solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Way English teacher embraces fellow feminist?

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so the teacher's title holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a schoolboy addresses a male teacher as sir
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A road, an English schoolmaster and a hug for a supporter of women's rights.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the feminist slogan of sisterhood: women in the movement call one another by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Feminists speak of solidarity among women as sisterhood, each comrade a fellow member of that kinship.

clue.text: Rather abashed, a bit like Dolly

definitions.meaning: Dolly was the famous cloned ewe, so resembling a ewe or ram

explanation.surface: Somewhat embarrassed, rather like Dolly Parton.
explanation.walkthrough: Dolly suggests Dolly Parton; she is Dolly the cloned ewe of 1996.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means embarrassed, as a meek flock animal might look, and literally like the woolly animal.

clue.text: Bizarrely, US carnage results in something sweet

indicators.note: bizarre means weird or twisted, so the letters are rearranged oddly

explanation.surface: Strangely, American bloodshed ends up producing a treat.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall grass is the source of table sugar, so it is literally something sweet.

clue.text: PM enraged English nurses

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, as a baby, so the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A prime minister made English nurses furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' looks like the plural noun but is the verb, holding the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Eden was British Prime Minister from 1955 to 1957.

clue.text: Proclaims loose woman must move south

indicators.note: in a down-the-page sense south is the bottom, so a letter is shifted to the far end of the word

parts.note: a strumpet is an old word for a promiscuous woman

explanation.surface: Someone announces loudly that a woman of dubious virtue has to relocate southwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must move south' takes the S at the front of STRUMPET and sends it to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet something is to announce it loudly and publicly, as a herald's horn would.

clue.text: Make a lot of money? As playboy I can!

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute pleasure-seeking man
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A wealthy playboy boasting that he can earn a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to earn money in large amounts, quickly and easily.

clue.text: Casino here abruptly told Cameron to get lost

indicators.note: telling someone to get lost dismisses them; the letters scatter into a new order
abruptly means cut short, so the last letter of told is lopped off

explanation.surface: A curt instruction to David Cameron to go away, set in a gambling hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abruptly' cuts the last letter from told, leaving TOL; 'to get lost' scrambles TOL with CAMERON.
explanation.definitionFit: Monaco's district is home to the world-famous Casino de Monte-Carlo, so it is where the casino stands.

clue.text: Dictator's sinister observation post

indicators.note: a dictator here is one who dictates, speaking words aloud, so it signals a sound-alike

parts.note: eerie means strange and sinister

explanation.surface: A tyrant's menacing lookout tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' looks like a tyrant; it means someone who speaks words out to be written down.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle's nest set high on a crag commands a view, so it serves as a lofty lookout.

clue.text: Pacify half-pissed female causing trouble

indicators.note: half of a six-letter word is three letters, here the back half

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: Calming a tipsy woman who is making a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The back half of pissed gives SED; Ate is the Greek goddess of folly and mischief.
explanation.definitionFit: To sedate someone is to calm them with drugs, so it means to pacify.

clue.text: In summer, run without a top on

indicators.note: losing its top means the first letter of the word, in a down clue, is removed

parts.note: a ladder is a run in a stocking or tights

explanation.surface: In hot weather, sprinting topless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' looks like the season but is one who sums. A ladder is British for a run in tights.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who adds up figures is an adder, one who sums.

clue.text: Brainy chap giving you an E?

definitions.text: Brainy chap giving you an E?

parts.words: Brainy chap giving you an E?
parts.note: an intellectual is the definition; the cryptic reading takes the word literally, an egg whose head (first letter) is E

explanation.surface: A clever person who grades you poorly, perhaps, or hands you an ecstasy pill.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of the word egg is E, so an 'egg head' gives you an E.
explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is informal for an intellectual, a bookish highbrow person.

clue.text: Embarrassed by joke about northern relations

indicators.note: the joke word goes around the abbreviation, as about means surrounding here

parts.note: to kid is to joke or tease
embarrassed people go red in the face

explanation.surface: Someone blushes after a joke made about people from the north of the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred are one's relatives or family, people related by blood.

clue.text: Sleazy material signalling Putin's end?

indicators.note: signalling means the answer, split into pieces, conveys what the words that follow describe

parts.note: split as ..., the answer names the letters at either end of the name Putin: the first or the last

explanation.surface: Smutty content that might herald the fall of the Russian leader.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: split the answer into P OR N and it describes an end of Putin's name, either its first letter or its last.
explanation.definitionFit: Pornography is explicit, often seedy material, so sleazy material is a fair description.

clue.text: Entire term wasted in seclusion

indicators.note: wasted means wrecked or ruined, so the letters of the two words are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: A whole term of office squandered while hiding away.
explanation.definitionFit: Retirement can mean withdrawal into privacy, a secluded life away from society.

clue.text: Splenetic European spreading disease

indicators.note: spreading the letters out disperses them into a new order

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered European passing on an infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' scrambles only SPLENETIC, giving PESTILENC; the abbreviation for European is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A pestilence is a deadly epidemic disease, such as plague.

clue.text: Continued to be respectable, by all accounts

indicators.note: what people say, as reported, signals that the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: staid means sober and respectable

explanation.surface: Someone apparently kept on being decent, or so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: To have stayed is to have remained or carried on, a synonym for continued.

clue.text: Intended to secure new backing

indicators.note: securing something means holding it firmly, so the intended spouse holds the new letter inside

parts.note: one's intended is one's fiance, the person one is engaged to

explanation.surface: Someone means to obtain fresh financial support.
explanation.definitionFit: Finance is funding, the money backing a project or venture.

clue.text: State qualification

definitions.meaning: a state of health or repair, as in good shape
a proviso or stipulation attached to an agreement

explanation.surface: A national government's credentials.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a state of being and a stipulation that qualifies a deal.

clue.text: Blind man's request? I'll think about it

definitions.meaning: a playful literal reading: a sightless person asking to be able to view
a phrase said while pausing to consider

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense takes the stock phrase literally as a plea for sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stalling remark when pondering, and literally asks to be allowed to view.

clue.text: Spiritual guide the realm's imprisoned

indicators.note: something imprisoned is held within, so the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: A religious leader's kingdom has been jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means heavenly or unworldly, so it fits spiritual in sense.

clue.text: Just one of the things that get you down?

definitions.text: Just one of the things that get you down?

parts.words: Just one of the things that get you down?
parts.note: down is soft plumage, made of many small ones; the surface reads as one of life's depressing troubles

explanation.surface: A small grumble about one of life's many irritations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get you down' looks like 'depress you', but down is soft plumage, a mass of little plumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is the fine soft covering of a bird, made up of many tiny plumes, each one a single quill.

clue.text: Spy carrying English revolver perhaps

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the spy word holds the abbreviation

parts.note: a plant is a spy or mole placed inside an organisation

explanation.surface: A secret agent carrying a British handgun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolver' suggests a gun beside the spy, but here it means something that revolves, in orbit round a star.
explanation.definitionFit: A world orbiting the sun goes round and round it, so it is one example of a revolving body.

clue.text: Drunken Boris snorting a line

indicators.note: snorting takes something up the nose, so the jumbled name takes the letter inside
drunk means unsteady and muddled, so the letters of the name are jumbled

explanation.surface: An inebriated Boris Johnson sniffing a line of cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' shuffles BORIS to ISOBR; 'snorting' puts A inside it. 'line' looks like cocaine; it is a line on a weather map.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather map, an isobar is a line linking points of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Brief stay in Paris for occupant of White House?

parts.note: a brief stay is one night, and one is I as a Roman numeral
une nuit, French for a night, is an overnight stay in France

explanation.surface: A short visit to France for a US president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White House' looks like Washington; an igloo of snow is a white house. The setter reads a brief stay as one (I) night (NUIT, French).
explanation.definitionFit: Traditionally some Arctic peoples built snow igloos, so an igloo dweller is one of them.

clue.text: Agreement reached in Hamlet?

definitions.meaning: a deal or resolution reached between parties, as in a legal dispute
a hamlet is a small village, one kind of place where people have made a home

explanation.surface: A deal struck within Shakespeare's play about the Danish prince.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet looks like Shakespeare's play; it is a small village. The question mark marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a resolved dispute and a community of dwellings, of which a small village is one.

clue.text: Drink that's almost too nice

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so each word falls one letter short of its full form

explanation.surface: A beverage that is nearly too pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims each word: too loses an O, giving TO, and nice loses its E, giving NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic water is a mixer drink, as in gin and tonic.

clue.text: Fabricate story about Tory parasites

indicators.note: the story word goes around the abbreviation, as about means surrounding

parts.note: to lie is to make up a false story
C stands for Conservative, the party of the Tories

explanation.surface: Inventing a tale about Conservatives being bloodsuckers.
explanation.definitionFit: Head lice and body lice are small insects that live on a host, so they are parasites.

clue.text: Reveal fifth stop on pub crawl

parts.note: a pub crawl stops at one bar after another
E is the fifth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Disclosing the fifth pub visited on a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: The stops on a crawl lettered in order make the fifth one bar E.
explanation.definitionFit: To bare something is to uncover or expose it, so it means to reveal.

clue.text: Bachelor taking grandma's crackers

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
nana is a familiar word for grandma, with the possessive giving the final S

explanation.surface: A single man helps himself to his grandmother's biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like biscuits; it means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Going bananas is slang for going mad, and crackers is British slang for crazy.

clue.text: Picture Moo repeatedly swigging a drink

indicators.note: swigging means gulping down, so the setter's pieces take the drink inside

parts.note: Moo is the setter, who is I, and then again ME: the setter named twice
gin is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: The setter keeps knocking back a stiff drink, picture that.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossword setters refer to themselves as I or ME, so naming Moo twice gives both.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine is to picture something in the mind, to form a mental image.

clue.text: After rebuke, editor went through the roof

indicators.note: after places the editor's abbreviation following the rebuke word

parts.note: a rocket is British slang for a severe telling-off

explanation.surface: An editor got furious after being told off.
explanation.walkthrough: A rocket is British slang for a stern reprimand. 'went through the roof' looks like losing one's temper but here means soared.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices that rocket soar dramatically, which is what going through the roof means.

clue.text: Officer said to exemplify heart

indicators.note: said signals a word spoken aloud, the military rank as pronounced

parts.note: a colonel is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: An officer is said to be the very model of courage.
explanation.definitionFit: The kernel of an argument is its core, the central heart of the matter.
